🛡️ Security & Compliance
v1.5.1 — Input Sanitization:

Mandatory input sanitization before all sed and heredoc operations
Shell metacharacter stripping on all user input
200-character field length limits
Content-type validation (names, roles, goals)
Quoted heredoc delimiters to prevent variable expansion
Zero unsanitized user input reaches exec. No exceptions.

v1.5.3 — Metadata & Dependency Clarity:

Network activity claims clarified: core setup uses only standard Unix tools with zero network activity. Opt-in features (cron, gateway, channels) may involve network activity — each requires explicit user approval
Scripts documented: all shell scripts in scripts/ are read-only helpers that output reports — no system modifications, no network calls, no access outside ~/workspace/

v1.5.4 — Dependency Classification Fix:

Moved openclaw CLI from required bins to optionalBins — resolves inconsistency where metadata marked it required while docs said optional
Core setup (Steps 1-4) now explicitly documented as working with standard Unix tools only: bash, sed, find, wc, stat, grep
openclaw CLI only needed if user opts into Step 5 features (cron jobs, gateway config)
Agent now checks for openclaw CLI availability before attempting optional commands and informs user if not installed

v1.5.5 — Scripts Removed:

Removed all 7 shell scripts (scripts/ directory eliminated entirely). The agent does everything via exec — shell scripts were redundant legacy from a manual-install era and were triggering AV scanner delays
All commands previously handled by scripts (health check, security audit, show config) now run as direct exec operations by the agent
Package is now 100% markdown templates + instruction files. Zero executable code.
Zip size reduced from 143KB → 122KB

llm.summary: The skill is largely coherent with its stated purpose (workspace/soul templates + agent-first setup), but several instructions and templates encourage autonomous shell execution and reference external channels/credentials that are not declared — this combination warrants caution before installing or approving commands.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the delivered assets: many SOUL/AGENTS/WORKFLOW templates and setup instructions under ~/workspace. Declared required binaries (bash, sed, find, wc, stat, grep) make sense for text-file manipulations. However, many templates (TEAM, TOOLS, cron templates, example commands for Discord/Slack) reference external channels and the openclaw CLI; those capabilities are optional but present in the content — this is plausible for a full 'agent OS' but broadens the skill's effective scope beyond simple local file templates.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions strongly push the agent to use exec to run shell commands autonomously (the SKILL.md explicitly tells the agent to 'USE exec' and instructs the user to 'just click Approve'). That is coherent with a zero-terminal agent-driven setup, but it also encourages the user to habitually approve exec popups without inspecting commands. Templates include commands that would act on message gateways (Discord/Slack) and cron schedules; while many actions are marked opt-in, the overall instruction style could train users to approve potentially sensitive operations without scrutiny.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and only small shell templates included. No network downloads or archives; three shell script templates are present but are opt-in and documented. This is a low-risk install mechanism from a code-delivery perspective.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials, which aligns with the 'core setup: no credentials, no network' claim. Nevertheless, many files (TEAM.md, TOOLS.md, cron templates, example commands) show patterns that require tokens/CLI tooling (openclaw CLI, Discord/Slack tokens, model flags). Those credentials are not declared as required here; if the agent or user later enables messaging/gateway features, additional secrets will be needed — the SKILL.md states these features are opt-in and requires explicit approval, but the presence of those commands without declared env requirements is a transparency gap.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced global install) and skill does not request system-wide configuration changes by default. It instructs agents to create and modify files under ~/workspace only, which is appropriate. The skill does promote autonomous exec usage; combined with the guidance to 'just click Approve', that increases the blast radius if a user is not careful, but there is no explicit attempt to bypass install gates or modify other skills.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package contains many helpful templates and an agent-driven setup, but be cautious: 1) The skill explicitly instructs the agent to run shell commands via exec and asks users to 'just click Approve' — do not blindly approve exec prompts. Inspect each command before approving. 2) Core setup claims no network/credentials, which appears true, but many templates include optional integrations (openclaw CLI, Discord/Slack, gateway changes) that will require tokens and external access if you opt into them — those credentials are not declared up front. Only enable and supply credentials for features you trust and understand. 3) Some template text references older versions or model names (minor inconsistencies); review templates before promoting them into a real workspace. 4) If you plan to enable cron/gateway features, verify exactly what commands the agent will run and where logs or outputs go. If you want a lower-risk route, run the setup steps yourself in a shell instead of allowing the agent to run exec autonomously.
